mission.title: The Hook
mission.description: Seek the Oracle's advice on winning over the Morpheus simulacrum.

npc.say: He has visited us a number of times. Sometimes he asks many questions; sometimes, none.
Well, I'm sure you'll figure something out. Don't you worry about it too much; you'll have a lot of other things to think about soon enough.
I... I wanted him to stop...stop dreaming his crazy dreams. I couldn't stand it anymore! He'd say such ridiculous things... As if there was any way out of this hell--any except the way he took...
He'll tell you all about that meanie Connor and poor Rod.

phase.briefing:
{player}, further operative attempts at convincing the Morpheus simulacrum to unlock the encrypted Zion archive for us have met with failure.
Although her messages are often deliberately vague, consultation with the Oracle has been known to inspire operatives to unexpected solutions in the past; additionally, the simulacrum was detected within the vicinity of the Oracle's home neighborhood, near Debir Court in Mara, slightly more frequently over the past four months than statistically "random" chance would dictate. Visiting the Oracle yourself may yield actionable information.

enter.say:
Gray really goes out of his way to justify sending us to the Oracle, doesn't he?
She's supposed to be in that apartment building...and the scale of these readings probably isn't lying.

talk.say:
Don't you worry; I won't tell Agent Gray that you and I get along. I'm not one to cookie and tell.
Now let me see... What could I tell you about Morpheus--I call him that, you know, it's simpler.
Hm... It's hard to make up someone's mind for them, kiddo--real hard. If you need him on your side, you've got to give him a reason that matters to him.

done.say: All right, that sounds like the cue that tea time is wrapping up.

phase.briefing: Operative, we have a report of a disturbance in the area; the description of the individuals seen could indicate E Pluribus Neo terrorists. We know that they consider that they have a special relationship with the simulacrum. This report bears investigating.

enter.say:
More like some of them just follow the sim wherever he goes, like it's some kind of messiah... I'd say "hey, whatever floats their boat," only those are terrorist boats, and the only direction I want them floating is straight down into the deep blue sea.
Huh... If there was something going on there before, it's over now. I'm not picking up any activity.

done.say:
Ew! Oh, just EPN... Now what do you suppose put them out of our misery?
Hey, I'm scanning unusual code on one of them.

A mash note? Wa-ait, that lipstick sealing it looks familiar. Let me scan the thing... Ahah! There's an embedded code... Doesn't look too tough to crack, just a base shift... Yep. A message. Here's what it says:
"Just dying to get in touch with you, dearie. But could you drop by our friend Connor Liebowitz's place on your way, and give him this message: 'He shouldn't have believed you.' He'll know what you mean.
Thank you, dear! Talk to you soon. Hugs and Kisses..."

phase.briefing:
Connor Liebowitz is a citizen recently released by the police, who held him under suspicion of murder; he'd been found loitering near the apartment complex of an acquaintance, Rod Plunkett, just after Plunkett was discovered dead outside the complex, having apparently fallen from the rooftop. The investigating officer had not been convinced by Liebowitz's claim that he had left Plunkett, very much alive, in good spirits after a friendly visit to his apartment; however, no evidence showing that the death was anything other than suicide came to light; Plunkett had been under treatment for manic-depressive behavior.
The packaging, writing style, and code of the letter you found was meant to appear to have been written for us to find by Veil, the Cypherite second-in-command. Such a convoluted method of contacting us would not normally be necessary for them. You are to convey the message specified in the letter to Connor Liebowitz, but remain alert for any suspicious activity.

enter.say:
I don't care if she is writing us love letters; I still don't trust her.
I hope Gray's got us covered on this. We're just passing the guy a simple message, but...
The code's showing just one bluepill in there.

objective.text: Give the message to Connor Liebowitz

talk.say:
Who are you? I've been released; you can ask the chief him--
"He shouldn't have..." What-- Who told you that? There was nobody there! Just Rod and I... Oh god... I know... I don't know what I was thinking--why I told him that...

done.say:
Whoa, dude just went off the hook...and all because we told him "he shouldn't have believed you"?
There's something else going on, but I think we need to leave Liebowitz there for the gents in the white coats.
Wait a second... The phone's ringing. Doesn't look like Liebowitz is going to pick up... Should we answer?
Leave the receiver, operative. We are tracing the call.

phase.briefing:
The appropriate agencies are being dispatched to Liebowitz's location, {player}.
This was evidently a demonstration of sorts by the Cypherites. Such an...inefficient display is somewhat typical of their methods. I will send you to the origin point of Veil's phone call, but end the meeting immediately if they will communicate nothing of substance.

enter.say:
Gee, nice of them to put on a show. There better've been some point to that.
The call was traced to that building. I've got a redpill signal in there.

talk.say:
Ohh, it's you.
Cryptos, that cute Machinist I was telling you about is here. You can come out now.

Forty-eight hours of police interrogation failed to extract a confession from Connor Liebowitz, but you did it with just a few words. Why did you succeed? Because we knew him. Rod Plunkett was someone we were watching closely--someone in danger of seeing past the careful facade of the Matrix. Tragically, this danger became reality when he told his irritable friend that gravity was a mere illusion, invented to weigh upon the souls of lesser men.
You wish the constructed Morpheus persuaded to assist you; I can accomplish this. Why will I succeed? Because I knew him. I ask only that, in the event that it does unlock the archive as a result, I am allowed to remove the RSI entries of any who are now Cypherites, before the Machines access the data themselves.

done.say: Seems like a tall order. Gray's going to want to hear about this.

It was we who verified the existence of New Zion, and laid the old city open to destruction. I do not require that you allow me first access of the captured signature database out of trust...but I do require it, nonetheless.
You are still wondering what Liebowitz did to Plunkett that has come to prey upon his mind? On the rooftop, he taunted him--mocked his making light of gravity--and ended by saying "Free your mind." Before we could reach him, Rod Plunkett leapt to his death.
A freed mind, indeed.

mission.finish:
It has been confirmed that Cryptos worked beside Morpheus in Zion; thus, it is possible that he will be able to exert some influence over the simulacrum. While Cryptos' offer of assistance is not selfless, neither is obtaining old signatures of current Cypherite operatives our primary objective. I consider it likely that his request will be approved.
Your handling of this affair is appreciated, {player}.
